claim: Manila Chinese Cemetery dates to the 1850s and holds temples, memorials and notable Chinese-Filipino burials.
quote: The Manila Chinese Cemetery is the second oldest cemetery in Manila, Philippines, after Paco Park.

claim: The mansion-tombs are functional houses with air conditioning, plumbing and kitchens, visited by families on weekends.
quote: They are fully functional homes fitted with modern conveniences such as air conditioning, bathrooms with hot and running water, flushing toilets, and kitchens.

claim: Built late 19th century for non-Catholic Chinese barred from Catholic burial; nicknamed Millionaires' Row and Little Beverley Hills.
quote: Popularly known as 'Millionaires' Row' and 'Little Beverley Hills', the Manila Chinese Cemetery was built in the late 19th century for the non-catholic Chinese who were denied burials in Catholic graveyards by the Spanish colonials.

claim: About a million people are buried in Manila North Cemetery, with thousands of informal settlers living among the tombs.
quote: Roughly a million people are buried in the Manila North Cemetery, with at least 7,000 living inside as caretakers or informal settlers.

claim: Families came as paid tomb caretakers and now live in makeshift houses built on top of mausoleums.
quote: Many families first came to live in the graveyards as caretakers, employed by the wealthy to maintain their clan's tombs or keep grave robbers away.

claim: Living residents serve as caretakers, tour guides and grave-tenders inside Manila North Cemetery.
quote: Living With the Dead in the Manila North Cemetery

claim: With nowhere else to live, some Filipinos sleep in and atop graves in Manila's cemeteries.
quote: Dwelling atop the dead: With no room to live, some Filipinos sleep in graveyards

claim: Paco Park is a circular former cemetery completed 1822 where Rizal was secretly buried; now hosts Friday classical concerts.
quote: Dr. Jose Rizal was secretly buried at 'Rizal Tomb' after his execution on December 30, 1896.

claim: Paco Park is a circular walled cemetery built for the colonial elite and cholera victims, later a national park.
quote: Paco Park is a recreational garden and was once a municipal cemetery built by the Dominicans during the Spanish colonial period.

claim: Rizal's sister marked his secret grave with a slab reading 'R.P.J.', his initials reversed.
quote: Inscribed on the slab were the letters 'R.P.J.', Rizal's initials in reverse.

claim: Fortune-tellers set up directly in front of Quiapo Church reading tarot, cards and palms for PHP 50-100, busiest Tuesdays and Fridays.
quote: just right in front of the facade of the church is where do all the stalls of fortune tellers can be seen.

claim: Vendors at Plaza Miranda sell amulets, herbal cures, love potions and odd 'mutya' stones beside the basilica.
quote: an organized chaos of jeepneys, street vendors, amulet sellers, and churchgoers.

claim: Anting-anting sold in Quiapo include cabbalistic medallions against accidents and brass charms against witchcraft.
quote: amulets and talismans sold in Quiapo include medallions with cabbalistic engravings that prevent general to specific accidents.

claim: A pagoda/Japanese-castle mansion in Quiapo built 1936-1941 by Japanophile Jose Mariano Ocampo, with a seven-storey tower.
quote: The Ocampo Pagoda Mansion is a mansion which resembles a pagoda configuration in Quiapo, Manila, Philippines. It was commissioned by Jose Mariano Ocampo and was constructed from 1936 to 1941.

claim: The semi-abandoned Quiapo mansion is filled with a sea of sculptures collected by the family.
quote: Secrets of the city: A sea of sculptures in an abandoned Quiapo mansion

claim: The Ocampo Pagoda now allows guided visits with a small gallery, reportedly around PHP 1,800 for up to 10 people.
quote: guided tours available by calling ... with a fee of P1800 for 10 people and below.

claim: San Sebastian is the only all-steel church in Asia, built 1891 from 52 tons of prefabricated steel shipped from Belgium.
quote: 52 metric tons of prefabricated steel sections were transported in eight separate shipments from Belgium.

claim: San Sebastian's Gothic Revival steel structure was assembled in Manila under Belgian engineering supervision.
quote: The San Sebastian Church - Gustave Eiffel's Church in the Philippines

claim: The claim that Gustave Eiffel designed San Sebastian was disproved via correspondence with his heirs.
quote: Was San Sebastian Basilica designed by Gustave Eiffel?

claim: The 1928 First United Building on Escolta, designed by Andres Luna de San Pedro (son of Juan Luna), was Manila's tallest when built.
quote: Designed by Andres P. Luna ... the building was the tallest building in Manila when it was completed in 1928.

claim: The Sylianteng family's adaptive reuse of the First United Building drove Escolta's creative rebirth.
quote: How First United Building Drives Escolta's Creative Rebirth

claim: HUB: Make Lab is an adaptive-reuse incubator and alternative shopping space for Filipino designers in the First United Building.
quote: HUB: Make Lab is an adaptive reuse, incubator space for creative startups and artists which also acts as an alternative shopping center.

claim: HUB: Make Lab sells curated Filipino-designer goods from stickers and postcards to fashion accessories.
quote: Hub: Make Lab in Escolta is a cool new space for unique finds

claim: Dapitan Arcade is a craft market selling home furnishings, decor and accessories in indigenous fibers, rattan, capiz and ceramics.
quote: Shop at the Dapitan Market Quezon City

claim: Dapitan Arcade has 60-100+ stalls of home decor, Christmas ornaments, ceramics and woodcraft and a strong haggling culture.
quote: this craft market totaling 60 vendors presently sells wares ranging from indigenous fibers, paper, rattan, capiz and ceramics, wood and metal.

claim: Visitors recommend Dapitan Arcade as a bargain destination for unique home decor and antique-style finds.
quote: DAPITAN ARCADE - All You SHOULD Know Before You Go 2026

claim: The museum displays part of Imelda Marcos's shoe collection (749 pairs as of 2020) in an 1860s former Spanish arsenal.
quote: The museum's main feature is a portion of criminal convict and former First Lady Imelda Marcos's shoe collection (749 pairs as of 2020).

claim: The Marikina Shoe Museum building previously served as arsenal, detention centre, motor pool and rice mill.
quote: Marikina Shoe Museum

claim: Imelda Marcos's ~3,000 pairs of shoes remain a symbol of the Marcos regime's excess.
quote: 3,000 pairs: The mixed legacy of Imelda Marcos' shoes

claim: Lolong's skeleton, the largest saltwater crocodile held in captivity, hangs in the museum's Ayala Reception Hall.
quote: the former Guinness World Records holder as the largest saltwater crocodile in captivity from September 3, 2011 until his death on February 10, 2013

claim: Lolong's skeleton is on public display at the National Museum of Natural History.
quote: Lolong's skeleton on display at Museum of Natural History

claim: Admission to the National Museum of Natural History is free.
quote: Admission is free - making it a perfect addition to your Manila itinerary.

claim: Bahay Tsinoy / Kaisa-Angelo King Heritage Center in Intramuros documents the history and contributions of ethnic Chinese in Philippine life.
quote: documents the history, lives and contributions of the ethnic Chinese in the Philippine life and history.

claim: Bahay Tsinoy charges roughly PHP 100 for adults and is often overlooked next to Intramuros' bigger sites.
quote: Entrance fee: PHP 100 for Adults, PHP 60 for Students

claim: Rizal was imprisoned at Fort Santiago for 56 days; ~600 bodies were found around Intramuros after the 1945 Battle of Manila.
quote: National hero Jose Rizal was imprisoned here for 56 days, from November 3 to December 29, 1896.

claim: Fort Santiago's dungeons, used as prison cells and a torture site, were opened to the public.
quote: Newly opened dungeon to give public 'complete Fort Santiago experience'

claim: The high-tide drowning legend is largely debunked since the dungeons sit above river level, though darker 'water dungeon' accounts persist.
quote: Fort Santiago: The Stone Sentinel of Manila's Martyrs

claim: The MMDA-operated Pasig River Ferry offers free rides along the river through central Manila.
quote: The Pasig River Ferry Service is a ferry service operating on the Pasig River in Metro Manila.

claim: A larger intermodal Pasig River ferry network with up to 18 terminals is slated for late 2026.
quote: New Pasig River ferry sailing by 2026 - PPA

claim: The Philippines' first locally built battery-electric ferry is being integrated into the Pasig River system.
quote: LOOK: The Philippines' first e-ferry has arrived.

claim: Sarao Motors, founded 1953 by Leonardo Sarao, made the jeepney a national icon; its jeepneys once outnumbered rivals ~7 to 1.
quote: Sarao Motors was established in 1953 by Leonardo Sarao, a former kalesa driver turned mechanic, as a small automotive shop with an initial budget of P700.

claim: The Sarao factory in Las Pinas welcomes visitors to watch jeepneys being hand-built.
quote: Sarao Jeepney Factory in Las Pinas

claim: Hidden Manila bars include Bank Bar 'hidden behind a 7-Eleven' and The Back Room 'behind a shoeshine chair'.
quote: hidden behind a 7-Eleven ... Positioned behind a shoeshine chair ... a Roaring Twenties-themed speakeasy.

claim: Poblacion speakeasies hide behind unmarked doors; Sari Sari sits behind a sari-sari store's Coca-Cola fridge and some require a DM'd code.
quote: Behind the Curtain: Best Speakeasy Bars in Makati

claim: The Penthouse 8747 is a Great Gatsby-era art-deco rooftop lounge in the Lepanto Building overlooking Ayala Triangle.
quote: Packed with loads of inspiration from The Great Gatsby era, this is a classic and chic art deco dream.

claim: The Penthouse 8747 is open nightly 4 PM to 2 AM, closed Mondays.
quote: The Penthouse 8747

claim: Cubao Expo, a former 1970s shoe arcade, is an indie creative enclave whose management screens out corporate chains.
quote: The admin strictly screens tenants to prevent hyper-commercial corporate takeover.

claim: Cubao Expo is packed with vintage stores, vinyl cafes, thrift shops and local bar-restos.
quote: Inside Cubao Expo: Quezon City's treasured oasis of vintage charm and modern vibrancy

claim: Smokey Tours, run by Bless the Children Foundation, walks visitors through Tondo, Smokey Mountain and Baseco, with proceeds funding a community school.
quote: Bless the Children Foundation in Manila carries out all Smokey Slum tours.

claim: Smokey Tours cost about PHP 1,500 per person per tour area, with private tours higher.
quote: the rate is P1500 per person per tour area, while a private tour ... is P3000 per person per tour area.

claim: The viral Thriller-dancing inmates are at a Cebu prison; dancing continues as rehab but public viewing has been intermittent.
quote: The CPDRC dancers are a collective of convicts at Cebu Provincial Detention and Rehabilitation Center, a maximum security prison in Cebu City.

claim: Cebu's governor has worked to bring back the dancing-inmates show to attract tourists.
quote: Cebu governor brings back 'dancing inmates' show

claim: Seng Guan Temple near Divisoria is a Buddhist temple with a stupa, columbarium of ash urns, dragon motifs and meditation rooms.
quote: It contains a stupa, a huge repository for urns of human ashes, several meditation rooms, and various shrines.

claim: Seng Guan is a serene urban Buddhist sanctuary with ornate carvings, red pillars and dragon motifs in Manila's Chinatown area.
quote: The Beauty of Seng Guan Temple: Manila's Urban Buddhist Sanctuary
